recipes.name: Thai Green Curry Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into 1 inch cubes
1 teaspoon fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped

steps.text: Pour 1 tablespoon soy sauce into a shallow dish. Place 1 tablespoon flour into a separate shallow dish. Toss chicken pieces in soy sauce, then in flour, coating pieces evenly.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken; cook and stir until browned, about 5 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium and stir in curry paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add green onions, garlic, and ginger; cook an additional 2 minutes.

Return chicken to the skillet, stirring to coat with curry paste. Stir in coconut milk, sugar, fish sauce, and remaining 1 tablespoon soy sauce; simmer over medium heat until chicken is tender and cooked through, about 20 minutes. Serve curry with cilantro leaves.

raw_recipe.headline: Thai Green Curry Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This Thai green curry recipe is made with tender chicken, green curry paste, coconut milk, ginger, and green onions for a deliciously fragrant dinner.

review.reviewBody: Yummo! It's a very authentic-tasting Thai curry chicken. Warning: the green curry paste varies A LOT by brand. I used Maesri brand: VERY hot (and we love hot foods). I only used 1.5 tbsp which was plenty. Also, the coconut milk should be a full-fat (not low fat) and also varies quite a bit by brand. I prefer the Chaokoh brand which is nice & thick. Both of these brands should be available at any decent Asian market. A couple of changes I made: 1. used boneless chicken thighs (not as dry as breast meat), 2. reduced sugar to 1 tsp. I also added carrots, onions, and peas (gotta sneak those vegies ;) This one's a keeper.

Save your time to measure curry paste and coconut milk, use 1 can (4 oz) of Maesri green curry paste and 1 can (14 fl oz) of coconut milk for cooking will have a good result. If coconut milk is too strong for you, reduce the amount or add some chicken stock.

All you need is to stir-fry your favorite vegetables in sequence depending on the cooking time. In my case, onions and carrots first, followed by fried tofu curds. Then I add some curry paste and coconut milk before adding tomatoes, green beans, and broccoli stems. Add the remaining of curry paste and coconut milk and let the sauce simmer until green beans are cooked to your liking. At the end, add zucchinis and broccoli florets a few minutes before you put the lid on and turn the heat off. 

Meat is almost unnecessary in this dish. If you like chicken, cut it in thin slices and marinate in some cooking oil and green curry paste. To ensure that chicken is tender and cooked thoroughly, stir-fry chicken as soon as vegetables are done. In a separated pan that is big enough for all ingredients, add some oil before adding chicken. Constantly stir chicken until only some pinkness shows. Add steamy-hot cooked vegetables in and mix all ingredients well.

Vegetables recommended for green curry: asparagus, bamboo shoot, bean sprout, broccoli, butternut squash, carrot, green bean, eggplant, mushroom, onion, snow pea, sweet pepper, tofu, tomato, zucchini, and etc.

Delicious!!! Took advise from other reviewers and made a few changes. Left out the flour and soy sauce altogether. Seasoned chicken with ginger, garlic and black pepper and sautéed. Chopped half an onion and sautéed with the garlic, fresh ginger and green onions. Added the entire small jar of green curry, cooked that for a couple of minutes then added back the chicken. Added 3 julienned large carrots along with 2 cans of coconut milk, 1Tbsp of sugar and fish sauce and cooked for 15 minutes. Sliced a small package of baby Bella mushrooms and cooked for another 5 minutes until tender. Garnished with cilantro and served with Jasmine Rice... Entire family loved it

I made a few tweaks, but first, an important safety warning. After I had browned the chicken and put it off to a plate, I added my curry paste (I was using Thai Kitchen brand) to the pan. It immediately started spattering furiously all over the stove, the countertop, the floor...my dog was right by the stove, so I had to shoo her out of the kitchen to stop her being hurt by the flying hot curry paste. I think this could be prevented by letting the skillet sit off the heat for a little while after removing the chicken and before adding the curry paste. That moment of panic aside, this was an excellent recipe! I used two tablespoons of curry paste for a half recipe, and the heat level was just about right for my husband and me. Eliminated the sugar entirely and didn't even miss it. I added julienned carrots at about the 15-minutes-left mark; they turned out perfectly; julienned bell pepper at the 5-minutes-left mark; they could have used another minute or two. But this was a great recipe, and I can see how it could be adapted in so many ways--so I'll definitely be making it again!

This was absolutely delicious. Changes I made - used one tbsp of green curry, one full fat can of coconut milk and maybe 3/4 cup or so water. It was very spicy for my teenagers (might have been my strong green curry paste from an Asian market) so I tempered it with about a cup of whole goat milk yogurt. Used about a half tbsp honey in place of the sugar. Squeezed a little lemon juice in at the end. My chicken pieces didn’t much get coated in the (gluten free) flour after the soy sauce (i ran out of the flour) but still turned out amazingly tender and moist. I used a small celeriac root, baby Bella mushrooms, a bit of the chopped stems of rainbow chard, and a zucchini for the veggies. Didn’t have fish sauce so I just used the soy sauce. Without adding any additional salt this curry had the most complex delicious flavors that my whole family raved about. Can’t wait to make it again, maybe next time with shrimp, bell peppers, mushrooms and use cauliflower rice as the base (I’m low carbing). Thanks!

Very good. I followed all directions. However, I doubled the curry amount Bc I wanted to taste more curry. I Added red and green bell peppers, and baby corn. Next time I would also add water chestnuts for more crunch. I wouldn't use so much sugar, or possibly just not use any Bc I hate having to add sugar to meals that aren't a dessert. And maybe less soy sauce Bc the green curry was salty enough, and less salt is better for health. This feed 7 people with modest portions. And a few of my friends were able to have a small second portion.

I also did a veggie version of this recipe, with tofu instead of chicken and then used a bag of frozen Asian style veggies and rice. Really, you can use whatever veggies or meat alternatives you want. I sauteed the tofu in a little olive and sesame oils, as well as some worchestershire sauce (only because I was down to my last TBSP of soy sauce). I put a little worchestershire sauce and veggie broth in with the frozen veggies and rice too. Once my tofu was nicely browned I removed it from the pan and used the same pan for the actual green curry sauce. I believe the only thing I omitted from the sauce was the fish sauce (and I used a lite soy sauce). After the veggies and rice were done cooking I put the tofu, veggies, rice, and sauce all together and served it like that. It was delicious!! Both my husband and I liked it very much (my husband said it was one of his favorite dishes now and that he will be requesting it a lot). I will definitely make sure to have enough soy sauce next time. I also may use different veggies - mushrooms would be good, as would baby corns, neither of which the frozen pkg had in it. I would also use more rice. Anyway, all of that can be tweaked to your preference. The sauce did turn out brownish, but who cares, it was so good and very easy too!!

Very tasty, for 4 servings I added 2 slices of pineapple when the spring onion goes in, and adding some pineapple juice during the last 20 minutes of cooking. With 10 minutes left I added some peppers. My wife said it was spot on (and can’t get more credit then that)

Great recipe that I used a few years ago, but recently made and it was perfect. I used a whole jar of Thai Kitchen curry paste, one can of coconut milk (approx. 13.5 fl oz), and added more garlic, ginger, and green onions that the recipe calls for because I like the flavors. I also added in some bamboo shoots. Came out really well, thanks so much!

My household loves this curry dish! The only reason I didn't give this recipe 5 stars is because I've made a few changes. My changes are as follows; I added an extra Tbsp of curry paste and ginger, 2 diced red Thai chilies and 2x 400ml cans of Coconut milk instead of 2 cups. I cut the sugar down to just 2 tsp
I added 1 1/2 cups chopped broccoli and 1 cup of chopped carrots to the mixture just after adding the coconut milk.

Increased the curry paste to 3 Tbsp and reduced sugar to 1Tbsp. At last 5 to 7 minutes of cooking I added snow peas and red peppers sliced thinly and a jalapeno with a few seeds. I also used chicken tenders cut into 1 inch pieces. The results were melt in your mouth chicken with just enough kick in the sauce. I have made this several times, always with great results.

I always make a recipe as close to written as possible the first time. I followed it pretty much spot on except for eyeballing some of the ingredients after the fact I tasted it and added maybe a teaspoon of garam masala and the next time I make it I’ll throw in some extra veggies and cut the double batch recipe from 4tb sugar to 1. Just a tad too sweet for my liking.

Very good! I use Mae ploy green curry paste , Chakoah coconut milk, and add green or red peppers, onion, sliced bamboo shoots, bean sprouts, chicken broth to the chicken. So much cheaper than the local thai restaurant!
I think the quality of the green curry paste makes a difference. I plan to make this recipe again and try a different brand. I used this brand.
This was great. I doubled the curry paste. I will be making this again!
I love green curry
Simply amazing! So easy and totally delicious

Was my 2nd time making this dish, 1st time I did the dreaded chicken thing, added a lot of time and mess and didn't improve the flavour in my opinion. I used chicken thighs, but wish I had used sliced breast instead, would have cooked quicker and more evenly. I added julienned carrots, red peppers and Chinese eggplant to simmer in the coconut milk simmer stage to extend the dish, give it colour and fiber. Could have worked well as a vegetarian dish. Also added a few kaffir lime leaves. Wish I had cut the sugar in half.
This was delicious! It's a little bit of work, not too much, and well worth a few minutes of extra effort. I'll be making this one again. I served it with a side of green peas, and everyone loved it.
As others said, it’s a bit sweet so next time I’ll cut back on the sugar but otherwise it was a nice dinner and resulted in clean plates all round.
